clue.text: Second class material

parts.note: ilk means kind or class, as in 'of that ilk'

explanation.surface: A remark about a second-rate grade of cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Silk is a fine fabric spun from the cocoons of silkworms, so it is a material.

clue.text: Having floated south across country duck departed marshes

parts.note: swam is the past tense of swim, having floated along

indicators.note: the duck leaves the country, which loses that letter

parts.note: Poland is a country
a duck in cricket is a score of nothing, O

explanation.surface: Having drifted across the country, a duck flew off over the marshes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'departed' strips the duck (a cricket score of nothing) out of the country; 'across' is only a joining word here.
explanation.definitionFit: Swamplands are tracts of permanently waterlogged ground, which is to say marshes.

clue.text: Landed on border when touring eastern county

indicators.note: in a down answer a piece on another sits above it
the first word goes round the eastern piece, holding it inside

parts.note: a bird that has lit has landed
a rim is an edge or border

explanation.surface: Someone touches down on a frontier during a tour of the east.
explanation.walkthrough: 'touring' wraps the landing word round E, and 'on' stacks that above the border, as a down answer allows. Leitrim is an Irish county.
explanation.definitionFit: Leitrim is a county in the Republic of Ireland, in the province of Connacht.

clue.text: Tent dweller must cut grass in a hurry

indicators.note: the tent dweller has to cut into the word for grass, sitting inside it

parts.note: to grass is slang for informing on someone, which is also to sing
a camper lives in a tent

explanation.surface: A camper has to mow the lawn quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grass' looks like the lawn, but it is the slang verb for informing. 'must cut' puts the tent dweller inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Scampering is running about quickly, as someone in a hurry does; the definition stands for the phrase describing someone moving fast.

clue.text: End snapped off shell one removed from whole cluster

indicators.note: the end of the word is broken away, losing its last letter

parts.note: a conch is a large spiral seashell

indicators.note: a letter is taken out of the following word

parts.note: entire means whole
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone snaps the tip off a seashell, removed from a complete collection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'End snapped off' cuts the H from CONCH, leaving CONC; 'removed from' takes I out of ENTIRE, leaving ENTRE.
explanation.definitionFit: To concentre, an old form of concentrate, is to bring things to a common centre, so it is to cluster.

clue.text: Give ear to order that needs taking up for bigwig

indicators.note: in a down answer, taking up raises the pieces so they read from the bottom

parts.note: lug is British slang for an ear
the OM is the Order of Merit

explanation.surface: Listen to a command that has to be carried out for a big shot.
explanation.walkthrough: LUG + OM read upwards gives the answer. The OM is the British Order of Merit.
explanation.definitionFit: A mogul is a powerful, important person, a magnate, from the Mughal emperors of India.

clue.text: Enounces eg middle three vowels specially for dramatist

indicators.note: the letters are specially arranged into a new order

parts.note: of the five vowels A, E, I, O, U, the middle three are E, I and O

explanation.surface: Someone pronounces the middle vowels with special care for a playwright.
explanation.walkthrough: ENOUNCES + EG + EIO make the thirteen letters that 'specially' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Eugène Ionesco was the Romanian-French playwright of the Theatre of the Absurd, author of Rhinoceros.

clue.text: National prime minister beheaded

indicators.note: having its head cut off, the name loses its first letter

parts.note: Benjamin Disraeli was a Victorian British prime minister

explanation.surface: A country's prime minister has been executed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'National' looks like an adjective but stands for a citizen of a nation.
explanation.definitionFit: An Israeli is a citizen of Israel, that is, a national of that country.

clue.text: Conditions of course exclude one getting medal ting medal

indicators.note: a letter is shut out of the preceding piece

parts.note: the going is the state of the ground on a racecourse
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Racing conditions shut someone out of a medal.
explanation.walkthrough: In horse racing the going is the condition of the course; taking out I leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Gong is British slang for a medal or decoration.

clue.text: French town reverses its refusal to proffer brief answer

indicators.note: the town turns round the pieces that follow, so they are read from back to front

parts.note: the French town's own word for no is non

indicators.note: a brief word is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: to proffer is to give or offer

explanation.surface: A French town goes back on its refusal to give a short reply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Its' points to the French town, so the refusal is the French one, not English no. 'brief' trims the last letter, and 'reverses' turns the whole run round.
explanation.definitionFit: Avignon is a town in Provence in southern France, once the seat of the popes.

clue.text: Love one's neighbour? Not much

parts.note: a neighbour is next to one
love is nothing, a zero score in tennis

explanation.surface: A biblical command to love one's neighbour, followed by a shrug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Love one's neighbour' looks like the commandment, but read it as the neighbour of love, which is nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Next to nothing is an idiom for a very small amount, hardly anything.

clue.text: Spaceman runs into gravitational effect a second time

parts.note: g is the symbol for acceleration due to gravity, as in pulling so many g

indicators.note: the runs are put into the middle of the other pieces

parts.note: once more, that is again
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: An astronaut feels the pull of g again during a run.
explanation.walkthrough: G + AGAIN gives GAGAIN, and 'into' puts R inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Yuri Gagarin, the Soviet cosmonaut, was the first man in space, in 1961.

clue.text: Fine example of cross discovered in trim little room in French church

indicators.note: the cross is found sitting inside the next two pieces

parts.note: to trim is to pare
a cell is a small room, as in a monastery or prison
X is the shape of a cross
en is French for in
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A model of a crucifix found in a neat cell in a French church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'discovered in' sets the cross between the trim and the little room, before the French and church pieces follow.
explanation.definitionFit: Par excellence means better than all others, the supreme example of its kind, so it serves as a fine example.

clue.text: Hostile to change initially, city takes on board disappointing outcome

parts.note: anti means opposed or hostile to

indicators.note: only the first letter of the word is used

parts.note: Lima is the capital city of Peru
in chess notation x records a capture, a piece taking on the board

explanation.surface: A city reluctant to change finally accepts a let-down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes on board' looks like accepting an idea, but chess notation writes a capture as x.
explanation.definitionFit: An anticlimax is a let-down after mounting expectation, a disappointing end.

clue.text: Grant to US college following promotion

indicators.note: the US college comes after the promotion

parts.note: an ad is an advertisement, a promotion
MIT is the Massachusetts Institute of Technology

explanation.surface: An award to an American university after a publicity drive.
explanation.definitionFit: To grant can mean to concede or acknowledge a point, which is to admit it.

clue.text: Chess player I can't fool twice with only one knight

indicators.note: to fool with something is to mess about with it, so the letters are jumbled
of the two knights in the doubled phrase, one is dropped
the phrase is written out two times

parts.note: taken as written, without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A chess player says he cannot be tricked twice while left with a single knight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twice' doubles I CAN'T to ICANTICANT; 'with only one knight' removes one of the two Ns (N is the chess knight); 'fool' rearranges ICATICANT into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A tactician is a skilful planner of manoeuvres, a word often used of a strong chess player.

clue.text: Old islander holding only son in cold regard

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

indicators.note: the lone son sits inside the other pieces

parts.note: to regard is to eye
lone means only or solitary

explanation.surface: An old native keeps an only son under a cold stare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' is just a joining word; 'in' puts the only son inside the cold regard. Ceylon is the old name for Sri Lanka.
explanation.definitionFit: A Ceylonese was a native of Ceylon, the former name of Sri Lanka, so an old islander.

clue.text: Drug-taking guard on duty with centre cleared infection

indicators.note: in an across answer one piece on another follows it
the middle of the word is emptied out, leaving only its first and last letters
the guard takes in the drug, holding it inside

parts.note: a sentry is a soldier on guard
E is ecstasy, a drug

explanation.surface: A sentry on duty takes drugs and picks up a bug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with centre cleared' empties the middle of duty; 'taking' puts the drug inside the guard, and 'on' places that after, as an across answer allows.
explanation.definitionFit: Dysentery is an infection of the intestines causing severe diarrhoea.

clue.text: When upset, rushed one's drink

indicators.note: in a down answer upset turns the letters over, reading from the bottom

parts.note: raced means rushed
one is I, and one's gives I'S

explanation.surface: Someone knocked over their drink while hurrying.
explanation.walkthrough: RACED + IS read upwards gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A sidecar is a cocktail of brandy, orange liqueur and lemon juice.

clue.text: Immigrant's child has two London postcodes

parts.note: N1 is the Islington postcode, with the digit 1 read as the letter I
SE1 is the Southwark and Waterloo postcode, again with 1 read as I

explanation.surface: The child of an immigrant has addresses in two parts of London.
explanation.walkthrough: London postcodes such as N1 and SE1 are letters plus a number; the digit 1 doubles as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Nisei is the Japanese term for an American or Canadian born to Japanese immigrant parents.

clue.text: Irish writer's works vanish first of all

indicators.note: the letters are worked into a new order
only the opening letter of the next word is taken

explanation.surface: All of an Irish writer's books disappear.
explanation.walkthrough: VANISH + A is rearranged by 'works'. 'Works' looks like the writer's output; it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Shavian means relating to George Bernard Shaw, the Irish playwright, so it serves for the possessive.

clue.text: Liberal on health body so upset by Dickensian school

indicators.note: in an across answer a piece on another follows it
the words are knocked over and their letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A Liberal disturbed by a health authority at a school out of Dickens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' rearranges HEALTHBODYSO into DOTHEBOYSHAL, and 'on' adds L at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Dotheboys Hall is the brutal Yorkshire school run by Wackford Squeers in Dickens's Nicholas Nickleby.

clue.text: Rugby's head to leave, as likely as not

indicators.note: the first letter is told to go

parts.note: sevens is the seven-a-side form of rugby, a version of the game

explanation.surface: A rugby team's captain is as likely as not to quit.
explanation.walkthrough: Rugby sevens is a fast seven-a-side version of rugby union.
explanation.definitionFit: Evens are betting odds of one to one, meaning an outcome is as likely as not.

clue.text: Grand to deliver frame

parts.note: G is slang for a grand, a thousand pounds or dollars
to deliver from something is to rid of it

explanation.surface: A thousand pounds to hand over a picture frame.
explanation.definitionFit: A grid is a framework of crossing bars, so it is a frame.

clue.text: Park at head of queue and sit back …

indicators.note: the park comes at the front of the queue

parts.note: a rec is a recreation ground, a public park
a line of people is a queue

explanation.surface: Someone at the front of a queue in the park leans back.
explanation.walkthrough: A rec is British slang for a recreation ground, a local public park.
explanation.definitionFit: To recline is to lean or lie back, so it is to sit back.

clue.text: … I'm holding that to be self-promotion

indicators.note: the first piece wraps around the second, keeping it inside

parts.note: I is the self, the ego, and 'm is the shortened am
'tis is the old shortening of 'it is', that thing to be

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue, someone insists their view is just self-advertisement.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links back to 24-across for the surface only. 'holding' wraps I'm round the old contraction for it is.
explanation.definitionFit: Egotism is excessive talk about and promotion of oneself.

clue.text: With strike off, Serge tried working

indicators.note: the letters are put to work in a new order

explanation.surface: Serge has a go at an industrial strike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With strike off' reads like taking strike action, but strike off is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To strike off is to remove from an official register, which is to deregister.

clue.text: Cross floor first, welcoming new preacher

indicators.note: the floor piece is placed ahead of the cross
the pieces take in the new arrival, holding it inside

parts.note: to floor someone is to knock them down, a KO or knockout
X is the shape of a cross

explanation.surface: An angry crowd crosses the floor to greet a newcomer to the pulpit.
explanation.walkthrough: KO goes 'first', ahead of X, and 'welcoming' puts N inside: K-N-OX.
explanation.definitionFit: John Knox was the fiery Scottish Reformation preacher who founded Presbyterianism.
